T1098.name: Account Manipulation
T1098.description: Adversaries manipulate accounts to maintain access. Very common in real-world AD attacks.

T1021.name: Remote Services
T1021.description: Adversaries use remote services for lateral movement. High frequency in enterprise incidents.

T1021.001.name: Remote Desktop Protocol
T1021.001.description: RDP used for lateral movement. Extremely common in enterprise environments.

T1550.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material
T1550.description: Pass-the-hash, pass-the-ticket. Core to AD lateral movement.

T1222.name: File and Directory Permissions Modification
T1222.description: ACL manipulation for privilege escalation. Moderately common.

T1558.name: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets
T1558.description: Kerberoasting, delegation abuse. Increasingly common in sophisticated attacks.

T1003.006.name: DCSync
T1003.006.description: Directory replication abuse. High impact, well-documented technique.
